messages:
alex: quick q about the /v1/rerank response shape — current example uses 

```json
{
  "items": [
    { "id": "doc_1", "score": 0.923 },
    { "id": "doc_2", "score": 0.923 }
  ]
}
```

are we ok with omitting `score` when it's not applicable, or should it always be present (null vs absent)?

sam: we landed on `null` in the runtime because omission broke some downstream mappers. null is explicit.

maya: FYI older JS clients assume a number and do `sum += item.score` so null will NPE unless they guard. that's a breaking change for some on-prem integrators.

tia: current prod behavior (pre-change) is: missing -> treat as -inf for ordering; null -> treat as -inf as well. So functionally similar but client parsing differs.

alex: ok so semantics for ordering are same, but shape differs. I think spec should require `score` key always present and allow `null` to mean no-score. makes clients easier.

sam: +1. also want to call out tie-breaker deterministic rule. runtime does: sort by (score desc treating null=-Inf), then stable by `id` ascending. there's also a canary flag that injects a bucketing salt for experimental rollouts.

maya: can we document the salt behavior? some teams depend on stable ordering across requests and the salt changes that.

sam: the salt only applies if you opt into `canary=true` header. it's not default. but adding a note is good.

alex: another ask — can we add an explicit `rank` integer in the response so clients don't need to re-sort locally? small addition but removes ambiguity. example:

```json
{
  "items": [
    { "id": "doc_1", "score": 0.923, "rank": 1 },
    { "id": "doc_2", "score": 0.923, "rank": 2 }
  ]
}
```

tia: +1 from me. easier for downstream. note: rank must be 1-indexed to match existing dashboards.

maya: also small nit — precision. some teams rely on 1e-6 diffs. do we send `score` as number double precision or string? sending strings preserves exact formatting.

sam: runtime currently emits float64 JSON numbers. switching to strings is annoying for consumers. let's keep numbers and call out `score_precision: "float64"` in spec if we want to be explicit.

alex: sounds good. i'll update the spec PR with three changes: (1) require `score` key present, allow null; (2) add `rank` int (1-indexed); (3) add note about canary salt and `canary=true` header; and (4) document score precision as float64. i'll ping reviewers.

alex: @maya @tia i'm going to push a tiny PR, will add a short changelog entry for backcompat.

deploy-bot: spec PR opened — https://github.com/redwood-inference/specs/pull/157 (alex)

maya: will review later today.

tia: on my review queue, will skim after standup.

alex: thanks all :thumbsup:
